combat_history.event: No combat use; inducted into IAF squadrons replacing the MiG-21.
combat_history.significance: Milestone for indigenous Indian fighter production.

modernization.description: Large Mk1A orders and development of the more capable Mk2.
modernization.impact: Builds a sovereign fighter pipeline and squadron numbers.

vulnerabilities.description: Limited range and payload versus heavier fighters.
vulnerabilities.context: A point-defence/light-multirole aircraft, not a long-range striker.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Point air defence and light multirole across Indian airspace, replacing the MiG-21.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Complements Su-30MKI and Rafale in the IAF.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The JF-17 is the Sino-Pakistani light fighter the Tejas competes with on capability and export markets.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Tejas vs JF-17 — South Asia's light fighters.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The Gripen is a more mature single-engine light fighter the Tejas aspires to match.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: How the Tejas measures up to the Gripen.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Both are light fighters chasing Global-South export orders.

doctrine.role: Indigenous light multirole fighter for point air defence and self-reliant fighter production.
doctrine.employment: Fly-by-wire delta for agile air defence and light strike, replacing the MiG-21.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Sovereign capability and industrial depth over peak performance.
doctrine.threat_context: Gives India numbers and a domestic fighter pipeline underpinning the future AMCA.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the JF-17, Gripen and FA-50.
